groups.title: Section A · 第 1 篇 · 1–4 题
groups.material:
M: Tonight, we have a very special guest. Mrs Anna Sanchez is a three-time Olympic champion and author of the new book To the Edge. Mrs Sanchez, thank you for joining us.
W: Thank you for having me.
M: Let's start with your book. What does the title To the Edge mean? What are you referring to?
W: The book is about how science and technology have helped push humans to the edge of their physical abilities. I argue that in the past 20 years we've had the best athletes the world has ever seen.
M: But is this a fair comparison? How do you know how, say, a football player from 50 years ago would compare to one today?
W: Well, you are right. That comparison would be perhaps impossible to make. But the point is more about our knowledge today of human biochemistry, nutrition and mechanics. I believe that while our bodies have not changed in thousands of years, what has changed is the scientific knowledge. This has allowed athletes to push the limits of what was previously thought possible.
M: That's interesting. Please tell us more about these perceived limits.
W: The world has seen sports records being broken that could only be broken with the aid of technology, whether this be the speed of a tennis serve or the fastest time in a 100-meter dash or 200-meter swimming race.
M: Is there any concern that technology is giving some athletes an unfair advantage over others?
W: That is an interesting question and one that has to be considered very carefully. Skis, for example, went from being made of wood to a metal alloy, which allows for better control and faster speed. There is no stopping technological progress. But, as I said, each situation should be considered carefully on a case-by-case basis.

groups.title: Section A · 第 2 篇 · 5–8 题
groups.material:
W: I've worked in international trade all my life. My father did so too before me. So I guess you could say it runs in the family.
M: What products have you worked with?
W: All sorts, really. I've imported textiles, machinery, toys, solar panels, all kinds of things over the years. Trends and demand come and go. So one needs to be very flexible to succeed in this industry.
M: I see. What goods are you trading now?
W: I now import furniture from China into Italy and foods from Italy into China. I even use the same container. It's a very efficient way of conducting trade.
M: The same container? You mean you own a 40-foot cargo container?
W: Yeah. that's right. I have a warehouse in Genova, Italy and another in Shanghai. I source mid-century modern furniture from different factories in China. It's very good value for money. I collect it all in my warehouse and then dispatch it to my other warehouse in Italy. Over there I do the same, but with Italian foods instead of furniture, things like pasta, cheese, wine, chocolates. And I send all that to my warehouse in China in the same freight container I use for the furniture.
M: So I presume you sell both lines of products wholesale in each respective country.
W: Of course. I possess a network of clients and partners in both countries. That's the main benefit of having done this for so long. I've made great business contacts over time.
M: How many times do you ship?
W: I did 12 shipments last year, 18 this year, and I hope to grow to around 25 next year. That's both ways, there and back again. Demand for authentic Italian food in China is growing rapidly. And similarly, sales of affordable, yet stylish wooden furniture are also increasing in Italy. Furniture is marginally more profitable, mostly because it enjoys lower customs duties.

groups.title: Section B · 第 1 篇 · 9–11 题
groups.material:
"Too many people view their jobs as a five-day prison from which they are paroled every Friday," says Joel Goodman, founder of the Humour Project, a humour consulting group in Saratoga Springs, New York. Humour unlocks the office prison because it lets adults bring some of their childlike spirit to the job.
According to Howard Pollio, professor of psychology at the University of Tennessee, Knoxville, an office with humour breaks is an office with satisfied and productive employees. Pollio conducted a study that proved humour can help workers excel at routine production tasks. Employees perform better when they have fun.
In large corporations with a hierarchy of power, there is often no outlet for stress. "Every company needs underground ways of poking fun at the organization," says Lynn N. Mark, a speaker on workplace humour for St. Mary's Health Centre in St. Louis.
Kodak's Rochester, New York branch discovered a way for its 20,000 employees to uncork their bottled-up resentments. Their 1,000-square-foot Humour Room features a toy store. Among the room's many stress-reducing gadgets, the main attraction is a boss doll with detachable arms and legs. Employees can take the doll apart as long as they put its arms and legs back in place.
Sandy Cohen, owner of a graphic print production business, created the Quote Board to document the bizarre phrases people say when under strict deadlines. "When you're under stress, you say stupid things," says Cohen. "Now we just look at each other and say, that's one for the Quote Board."

groups.title: Section B · 第 2 篇 · 12–15 题
groups.material:
Public interest was aroused by the latest discovery of a changed gene in obese mice. The news was made known by Rockefeller University geneticist Jeffrey Friedman. The researchers believe this gene influences development of a hormone that tells the organism how fat or full it is. Those with the changed gene may not sense when they have eaten enough or if they have sufficient fatty tissue, and thus can't tell when to stop eating.
The researchers also reported finding a gene nearly identical to the mouse obesity gene in humans. The operation of this gene in humans has not yet been demonstrated, however. Still, professionals like University of Vermont psychologist Esther Rothblum reacted enthusiastically: "This research indicates that people really are born with a tendency to have a certain weight, just as they are to have a particular skin color or height."
Actually, behavioral geneticists believe that less than half of the total weight variation is programmed in the genes, while height is almost entirely genetically determined.
Whatever role genes play, Americans are getting fatter. A survey by the Center for Disease Control found that obesity has increased greatly over the last 10 years. Such rapid change underlines the role of environmental factors, like the abundance of rich foods, in Americans' overeating.
The Center for Disease Control has also found that teens are far less physically active than they were even a decade ago. Accepting that weight is predetermined can relieve guilt for overweight people. But people's belief that they cannot control their weight can itself contribute to obesity.

groups.title: Section C · 第 1 篇 · 16–18 题
groups.material:
Qualities of a relationship, such as openness, compassion, and mental stimulation are of concern to most of us regardless of sex, but—judging from the questionnaire response—they are more important to women than to men.
Asked to consider the ingredients of close friendship, women rated these qualities above all others. Men assigned a lower priority to them in favor of similarity in interests, selected by 77% of men, and responsiveness in a crisis, chosen by 61% male respondents. Mental stimulation, ranked third in popularity by men as well as women, was the only area of overlap. Among men, only 28% named openness as an important quality; caring was picked by just 23%.
It is evident by their selections that when women speak of close friendships they are referring to emotional factors, while men emphasize the pleasure they find in a friend's company. That is, when a man speaks of "a friend" he is likely to be talking about someone he does things with—a teammate, a fellow hobbyist, a drinking buddy. These activities are the fabric of the friendship; it is a "doing" relationship in which similarity in interests is the key bond. This factor was a consideration of less than 11% of women. Women opt for a warm, emotional atmosphere where communication flows freely; activity is mere background.
Lastly, men, as we have seen, have serious questions about each other's loyalty. Perhaps this is why they placed such strong emphasis on responsiveness in a crisis—"someone I can call on for help." Women, as their testimonies indicate, are generally more secure with each other and consequently are more likely to treat this issue lightly. In follow-up interviews this was confirmed numerous times as woman after woman indicated that "being there when needed was taken for granted."
As for the hazards of friendship, more than a few relationships have been shattered because of cutthroat competition and feelings of betrayal. This applies to both men and women, but unequally. In comparison, nearly twice as many men complained about these issues as women. Further, while competition and betrayal are the main thorns to female friendship, men are plagued in almost equal amounts by two additional issues: lack of frankness and a fear of appearing unmanly. Obviously, for a man, a good friendship is hard to find.

groups.title: Section C · 第 2 篇 · 19–21 题
groups.material:
The partial skeletons of more than 20 dinosaurs and the scattered bones of about 300 more have been discovered in Utah and Colorado at what is now the Dinosaur National Monument. Many of the best specimens may be seen today at museums of natural history in the larger cities of the United States and Canada. This dinosaur pit is the largest and best preserved deposit of dinosaurs known today.
Many people get the idea from the mass of bones in the pit wall that some disaster such as a volcanic explosion or a sudden flood killed a whole herd of dinosaurs in this area. This could have happened but it probably did not.
The main reasons for thinking otherwise are the scattered bones and the thickness of the deposit.
In other deposits where the animals were thought to have died together, the skeletons were usually complete and often all the bones were in their proper places. Rounded pieces of fossil bone have been found here. These fragments got their smooth round shape by rolling along the stream bottom.
In a mass killing, the bones would have been left on the stream or lake bottom together at the same level. But in this deposit, the bones occur throughout a zone of sandstone about 12 feet thick.
The mixture of swamp dwellers and dry-land types also seems to indicate that the deposit is a mixture from different places.
The pit area is a large dinosaur graveyard, not a place where they died. Most of the remains probably floated down an eastward flowing river until they were left on a shallow sandbar. Some of them may have come from far-away dry-land areas to the west. Perhaps they drowned trying to cross a small stream or were washed away during floods. Some of the swamp dwellers may have got stuck in the very sandbar that became their grave; others may have floated for miles before being stranded.
Even today similar events take place. When floods come in the spring, sheep, cattle and deer are often trapped by rising waters and often drown. Their dead bodies float downstream until the flood recedes and leaves them stranded on a bar or shore where they lie, half buried in the sand, until they decay. Early travelers on the Missouri river reported that shores and bars were often lined with the decaying bodies of buffalo that had died during spring floods.

groups.title: Section C · 第 3 篇 · 22–25 题
groups.material:
I would like particularly to talk about the need to develop a new style of aging in our own society.
Young people in this country have been accused of not caring for their parents the way they would have in the old country. And this is true. But it is also true that old people have been influenced by an American ideal of independence and autonomy. So we live alone, perhaps on the verge of starvation, in time without friends, but we are independent.
This standard American style has been forced on every ethnic group, although there are many groups for whom the ideal is not practical. It is a poor ideal and pursuing it does a great deal of harm. This ideal of independence also contains a tremendous amount of unselfishness.
In talking to today's young mothers. I have asked them what kind of grandmothers they think they are going to be. I hear devoted, loving mothers say that when they are through raising their children, they have no intention of becoming grandmothers. They are astonished to hear that in most of the world throughout most of its history, families have been three- or four-generation families, living under the same roof.
We have over-emphasized the small family unit—father, mother, small children. We think it is wonderful if grandma and grandpa, if they're still alive, can live alone. We have reached the point where we think the only thing we can do for our children is to stay out of their way and the only thing we can do for our daughter-in-law is to see as little of her as possible.
Old people's nursing homes, even the best run, are filled with older people who believe the only thing they can do for their children is to look cheerful when they come to visit. So in the end, older people have to devote all their energies to "not being a burden".
We are beginning to see what a tremendous price we've paid for our emphasis on independence and autonomy. We've isolated old people and we've cut off the children from their grandparents.
One of the reasons we have as bad a generation gap today as we do is that grandparents have stepped out. Young people are being deprived of the thing they need most—perspective, to know why their parents behave so peculiarly and why their grandparents say the things they do.

questions.prompt: What do we learn about Anna Sanchez?
options: She is a great athlete.
She is a famed speaker.
She is a famous scientist.
She is a noted inventor.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do we learn about Anna Sanchez? 

 【翻译】 关于Anna Sanchez我们了解到什么? 
 A)  她是一名优秀的运动员。 
 B)  她是一位著名的演讲者。 
 C)  她是一位著名的科学家。 
 D)  她是一位知名的发明家。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） She is a great athlete. 
 【定位】 P1 Mrs Anna Sanchez is a three-time Olympic champion and author of the new book To the Edge. 
 安娜·桑切斯女士是一位三届奥运冠军，也是新书《抵达极限》的作者。 

 【信号】 开场介绍嘉宾的直接陈述 。主持人开场介绍嘉宾时直接给出身份 a three-time Olympic champion and author，这是访谈交代人物的固定位置，无需转折提示，听到头衔即定位。 

 【替换】 a three-time Olympic champion ↔ a great athlete 三届奥运冠军=了不起的运动员（具体→概括） 

 【排除】 B) 过度推断 她确是 author of the new book，又正在节目里侃侃而谈，易让人误推成 She is a famed speaker.；但『写书的人/受访者』不等于『著名演说家』，原文从未称她为 speaker。  借用原文：author of the new book To the Edge 

 C) 原词陷阱 访谈通篇是 science、scientific knowledge，极易让人听到『科学』就选 She is a famous scientist.；但她是『谈论科学如何帮助运动员』的运动员，不是科学家本人。  借用原文：what has changed is the scientific knowledge 

 D) 原词陷阱 她反复谈 science and technology，易诱人选 She is a noted inventor.；但谈论科技的人不等于发明科技的人，原文未称她为 inventor。  借用原文：science and technology have helped push humans to the edge

questions.prompt: What is the woman's book mainly about?
options: How knowledge of human biochemistry has been evolving.
How nutrition helps athletes' performance in competitions.
How scientific training enables athletes to set new records.
How technology has helped athletes to scale new heights.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What is the woman's book mainly about? 

 【翻译】 这位女士的书主要讲什么? 
 A)  人类生物化学知识是如何演变的。 
 B)  营养如何帮助运动员在比赛中取得好成绩。 
 C)  科学训练如何使运动员创造新纪录。 
 D)  技术如何帮助运动员攀登新高度。 

 【答案】 D （主旨题） How technology has helped athletes to scale new heights. 
 【定位】 P4 The book is about how science and technology have helped push humans to the edge of their physical abilities. 
 这本书讲的是科学与技术如何帮助人类把自身的身体能力推向极限。 

 【信号】 被问书名含义时的总括应答 。主持人请她解释书名，她答 The book is about how…——The book is about 是直接给主旨的总括句，正是被问者对『书讲什么』的应答落点。 

 【替换】 science and technology have helped push humans to the edge of their physical abilities ↔ technology has helped athletes to scale new heights 推向身体极限=登上新高度（同义改写） 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 How knowledge of human biochemistry has been evolving. 借原文 human biochemistry 一词设套；biochemistry 只是书里提到的一个知识侧面，绝非全书主旨，以偏概全。  借用原文：our knowledge today of human biochemistry, nutrition and mechanics 

 B) 原词陷阱 How nutrition helps athletes' performance in competitions. 借原文 nutrition 设套；营养只是书里并列提到的一项，不能代表全书，范围被缩小。  借用原文：human biochemistry, nutrition and mechanics 

 C) 偷换概念 How scientific training enables athletes to set new records. 杂糅了原文的 scientific 与后文 sports records being broken；但书主旨是『科技把人推向极限』这一宽命题，破纪录只是其表现之一，且原文强调的是 technology 而非 training。  借用原文：sports records being broken that could only be broken with the aid of technology

questions.prompt: What has changed in the past thousands of years?
options: Our physical structures.
Our scientific knowledge.
Our biochemical process.
Our concept of nutrition.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What has changed in the past thousands of years? 

 【翻译】 在过去数千年里什么发生了变化? 
 A)  我们的身体结构。 
 B)  我们的科学知识。 
 C)  我们的生物化学过程。 
 D)  我们的营养概念。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） Our scientific knowledge. 
 【定位】 P6 I believe that while our bodies have not changed in thousands of years, what has changed is the scientific knowledge. 
 我认为，几千年来我们的身体并没有改变，真正改变的是科学知识。 

 【信号】 while 引导的『没变 vs 变了』对比 。while our bodies have not changed 与 what has changed is the scientific knowledge 形成正反对比，while 是让步对比信号；题问『变了什么』，落点在对比里『变了』的那一侧。 

 【替换】 what has changed is the scientific knowledge ↔ Our scientific knowledge. 原句明点 scientific knowledge=选项几乎原词 

 【排除】 A) 与原文相反 原文说 our bodies have not changed，身体属于『没变』的一侧；Our physical structures. 正是身体结构，恰好答反——题问的是『变了』的，它却是『没变』的。  借用原文：our bodies have not changed in thousands of years 

 C) 原词陷阱 Our biochemical process. 借原文 human biochemistry 设套；biochemistry 只是『知识』所含的内容之一，原文明说变的是 scientific knowledge，不是某个生化过程本身。  借用原文：our knowledge today of human biochemistry, nutrition and mechanics 

 D) 原词陷阱 Our concept of nutrition. 借原文 nutrition 一词诱选；营养同样只是知识涵盖的内容之一，并非原文点名『变了』的那一项。  借用原文：human biochemistry, nutrition and mechanics

questions.prompt: What is the man's concern about the use of technology in sports competitions?
options: It may increase the expenses of sports competitions.
It may lead to athletes' over-reliance on equipment.
It may give an unfair advantage to some athletes.
It may change the nature of sports competitions.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What is the man's concern about the use of technology in sports competitions? 

 【翻译】 这位男士对在体育比赛中使用技术有什么担忧? 
 A)  它可能会增加体育比赛的费用。 
 B)  它可能导致运动员过度依赖设备。 
 C)  它可能给某些运动员带来不公平的优势。 
 D)  它可能改变体育比赛的性质。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） It may give an unfair advantage to some athletes. 
 【定位】 P9 Is there any concern that technology is giving some athletes an unfair advantage over others? 
 会不会有这样的担忧：技术正在让某些运动员相比其他人获得不公平的优势？ 

 【信号】 concern 一词直接标示担忧+由男士问出 。男士的问句以 Is there any concern that… 直接打出 concern 信号，且本题问『男士的担忧』，落点正在他这句问话，而非女士的回答。 

 【替换】 technology is giving some athletes an unfair advantage over others ↔ It may give an unfair advantage to some athletes 近原句重述，仅时态/语序微调 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 It may increase the expenses of sports competitions. 谈比赛开支，全篇没有任何关于花钱/成本的内容，纯属凭空添加。 
 B) 过度推断 女士回答里提到 Skis 这类装备，易诱人推出 It may lead to athletes' over-reliance on equipment.；但原文谈滑雪板是讲技术进步，从未说运动员『过度依赖装备』，是凭装备话题硬推的隐患。  借用原文：Skis, for example, went from being made of wood to a metal alloy 

 D) 过度推断 It may change the nature of sports competitions. 说法宏大，像是对 unfair advantage 的拔高引申；但男士担忧的是『公平』这一具体点，原文从未说科技会『改变比赛本质』。

questions.prompt: What does the woman think is required to be successful in international trade?
options: Experience.
Flexibility.
Family background.
Business connections.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the woman think is required to be successful in international trade? 

 【翻译】 这位女士认为在国际贸易中取得成功需要什么? 
 A)  经验。 
 B)  灵活性。 
 C)  家庭背景。 
 D)  商业关系。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） Flexibility. 
 【定位】 P3 Trends and demand come and go. So one needs to be very flexible to succeed in this industry. 
 潮流和需求来来去去。所以要在这一行成功，人就必须非常灵活。 

 【信号】 needs to be… to succeed 的"必需"句式 。答案信号是表"必需"的句式 one needs to be very flexible to succeed in this industry——needs to be… 直接点出成功所必须具备的那一项，正是 Q5"required to be successful"对应的落点。 

 【替换】 one needs to be very flexible ↔ Flexibility. 形容词 flexible 转名词 Flexibility 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 Experience. 是凭常识"显然要有"的项，但录音从没说成功"需要"经验；她只在讲资历时旁及做了一辈子，并未把经验列为"required to be successful"。 
 C) 原词陷阱 Family background. 听着像录音里 it runs in the family(这行在家里传承)，于是"听到家庭就想选"；但那句只是介绍她的出身经历，回答的是"她怎么入行"，并非"成功所必需"，与 Q5 问的不是一回事。  借用原文：it runs in the family 

 D) 原词陷阱 Business connections. 对应录音后文 I've made great business contacts over time，但她把人脉说成"做久了的好处"(benefit)，是结果不是"成功的必需条件"；且这话出现在 Q7 附近，搬到 Q5 来答属张冠李戴。  借用原文：I've made great business contacts over time

questions.prompt: What does the woman say is special about her way of doing trade?
options: Buying directly from factories.
Shipping goods in bulk by sea.
Having partners in many parts of the world.
Using the same container back and forth.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the woman say is special about her way of doing trade? 

 【翻译】 这位女士说她的贸易方式有什么特别之处? 
 A)  直接从工厂购买。 
 B)  通过海运批量运输货物。 
 C)  在世界许多地方都有合作伙伴。 
 D)  来回使用同一个集装箱。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） Using the same container back and forth. 
 【定位】 P5 I now import furniture from China into Italy and foods from Italy into China. I even use the same container. It's a very efficient way of conducting trade. 
 我现在把家具从中国进口到意大利，把食品从意大利进口到中国。我甚至用同一个集装箱。这是一种非常高效的贸易方式。 

 【信号】 even 的强调语气 + "非常高效"评价 。答案信号是强调词 I even use the same container 里的 even(甚至)，加上紧跟的 It's a very efficient way 自评"非常高效"——even 把这个做法特意拎出来当作不寻常之处，正是 Q6 的"special"。 

 【替换】 I even use the same container ↔ Using the same container back and forth. "用同一集装箱"概括为"往返复用" 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 Buying directly from factories. 听着像录音 I source mid-century modern furniture from different factories，于是"听到工厂就想选"；但从工厂进货是常规做法、她也没说这点特别，与 Q6 问的"special"不符。  借用原文：from different factories in China 

 B) 未提及 Shipping goods in bulk by sea. 是外贸最普通的做法，听着合理，但录音通篇没说"海运"或"大宗"，属凭常识脑补、原文未提。 
 C) 原词陷阱 Having partners in many parts of the world. 借用了录音 I possess a network of clients and partners 的"伙伴"原词，但录音说的合作伙伴只在 in both countries(两国)，选项却扩成 many parts of the world(世界许多地方)，范围被放大且这是 Q7 附近的内容，搬来答 Q6 也不对路。  借用原文：partners in both countries

questions.prompt: What does the woman have in both Italy and China?
options: Warehouses.
Factories.
Investors.
Retailers.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the woman have in both Italy and China? 

 【翻译】 这位女士在意大利和中国都拥有什么? 
 A)  仓库。 
 B)  工厂。 
 C)  投资者。 
 D)  零售商。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） Warehouses. 
 【定位】 P7 I have a warehouse in Genova, Italy and another in Shanghai. 
 我在意大利的热那亚有一个仓库，在上海还有另一个。 

 【信号】 I have… and another in… 的两地并列 。答案信号是"两地各有一个"的并列句式 I have a warehouse in Genova, Italy and another in Shanghai——a warehouse… and another… 明确说出两国各有一个仓库，正对 Q7 的"in both Italy and China"。 

 【替换】 a warehouse in Genova, Italy and another in Shanghai ↔ Warehouses. 单数 a warehouse + another 合为复数 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 Factories. 盗用录音 from different factories in China 的高频原词，"听到工厂就想选"；但工厂是她进货的对象、属于别人，并非她在两地都"拥有"的东西，与 Q7 的 have 不符。  借用原文：from different factories in China 

 C) 未提及 Investors. 全篇没有出现，录音里没有任何关于投资人的内容，纯属未提及。 
 D) 与原文相反 Retailers.(零售商)与录音相反：M 说她 sell both lines of products wholesale(批发销售)、她答 Of course，说明走的是批发渠道，不是零售；且她"拥有"的是仓库，不是零售商。  借用原文：sell both lines of products wholesale

questions.prompt: What does the woman say makes furniture marginally more profitable?
options: Trendy style.
Unique design.
Lower import duties.
Lower shipping costs.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the woman say makes furniture marginally more profitable? 

 【翻译】 这位女士说什么使家具的利润略微提高? 
 A)  时尚的风格。 
 B)  独特的设计。 
 C)  较低的进口关税。 
 D)  较低的运输成本。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） Lower import duties. 
 【定位】 P11 Furniture is marginally more profitable, mostly because it enjoys lower customs duties. 
 家具的利润略微高一些，主要是因为它享有较低的关税。 

 【信号】 mostly because 的因果信号 。答案信号是因果连词 mostly because it enjoys lower customs duties 里的 because——它直接引出"利润略高"的原因，正是 Q8 要的归因落点。 

 【替换】 lower customs duties ↔ Lower import duties. customs duties = import duties 同义 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 Trendy style. 听着像录音 affordable, yet stylish wooden furniture 的 stylish，于是"听到时髦就想选"；但那句讲的是家具在意大利"销量增长"(好卖)，不是"利润略高的原因"，把"好卖"当成了"更赚钱"。  借用原文：affordable, yet stylish wooden furniture 

 B) 未提及 Unique design. 与 A 同属"产品卖点"类，但录音根本没说家具"设计独特"，更没把它当作利润高的原因，属未提及。 
 D) 偷换概念 Lower shipping costs.(更低运费)与 C 极易混，但录音明说原因是 lower customs duties(关税)，从未把利润高归于运费；shipping 一词虽在别处出现，这里却答非所问。  借用原文：lower customs duties

questions.prompt: What does the passage say about humour in the workplace?
options: It helps employees to reduce their stress.
It prevents employees from feeling bored.
It strengthens harmony among employees.
It helps employees to view things positively.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the passage say about humour in the workplace? 

 【翻译】 文章关于职场幽默说了什么? 
 A)  它帮助员工减轻压力。 
 B)  它防止员工感到无聊。 
 C)  它增强员工之间的和谐。 
 D)  它帮助员工积极地看待事物。 

 【答案】 A （主旨题） It helps employees to reduce their stress. 
 【定位】 P1 Humour unlocks the office prison because it lets adults bring some of their childlike spirit to the job. 
 幽默打开了办公室这座监狱，因为它让成年人把一些孩童般的精神带到工作中。 

 【信号】 开篇点题句 + 后文减压主线 。首段把职场比作 a five-day prison from which they are paroled every Friday（把工作日比作要熬到周五才获释的监狱），紧接一句 Humour unlocks the office prison——开篇用"幽默解开办公室监狱"点题；其后各段（P3 谈 outlet for stress、P4 谈 uncork their bottled-up resentments）持续指向缓解压力，主旨主线就是"减压"。 

 【替换】 Humour unlocks the office prison ↔ reduce their stress 比喻还原为字面 
 there is often no outlet for stress ↔ reduce their stress 提供出口=减压 

 【排除】 B) 未提及 It prevents employees from feeling bored. 说幽默防止员工无聊，但全篇只讲减压、释放怨气、提升效率，从未提"无聊（bored）"这回事，是凭空添加的功能。 
 C) 原词陷阱 It strengthens harmony among employees. 借了文中反复出现的 employees 一词制造熟悉感，但录音谈的是减压与效率，没有讲幽默增进员工间"和谐（harmony）"，方向跑偏。  借用原文：satisfied and productive employees 

 D) 过度推断 It helps employees to view things positively. 看似与"幽默"沾边，但录音从未说幽默让人"积极看待事物（view things positively）"，这是从减压主题再往前推一步的引申，原文没有落脚点。

questions.prompt: What does the study by Howard Pollio show?
options: Weekends are conducive to reducing stress.
Humor is vital to interpersonal relationships.
All workers experience some emotional stress.
Humor can help workers excel at routine tasks.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the study by Howard Pollio show? 

 【翻译】 Howard Pollio的研究表明了什么? 
 A)  周末有助于减轻压力。 
 B)  幽默对人际关系至关重要。 
 C)  所有员工都会经历一些情绪压力。 
 D)  幽默可以帮助员工在日常工作中表现出色。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） Humor can help workers excel at routine tasks. 
 【定位】 P2 Pollio conducted a study that proved humour can help workers excel at routine production tasks. 
 波利奥做了一项研究，证明幽默能帮助员工在日常生产任务上表现出色。 

 【信号】 专名 Pollio + proved 引出结论 。录音先报出处 According to Howard Pollio，随后 Pollio conducted a study that proved 用 proved 直接引出研究结论——人名加"证明了"是答案句的明确信号，结论就在这句里。 

 【替换】 humour can help workers excel at routine production tasks ↔ Humour can help workers excel at routine tasks 近乎逐词对应 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 Weekends are conducive to reducing stress. 里的 weekends 容易让人联想到首段 paroled every Friday 那个比喻，但录音只是用周五打比方，从没说"周末有助于减压"这个论断，更不是 Pollio 研究的结论。  借用原文：paroled every Friday 

 B) 未提及 Humor is vital to interpersonal relationships. 谈幽默对人际关系重要，听上去合理，但 Pollio 的研究讲的是"工作表现"，全篇也没把幽默与"人际关系（interpersonal relationships）"挂钩，属无中生有。 
 C) 过度推断 All workers experience some emotional stress. 用 All 把范围放到"所有员工"，录音虽多次谈压力，却没说"所有员工都有情绪压力"，更不是 Pollio 研究的结论；绝对词常是陷阱。  借用原文：there is often no outlet for stress

questions.prompt: What can Kodak's employees do in the Humour Room?
options: Smash the toys to release their bottled-up resentments.
Take the boss doll apart as long as they reassemble it.
Design and install stress-reducing gadgets.
Strike at the boss doll as hard as they like.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What can Kodak's employees do in the Humour Room? 

 【翻译】 Kodak的员工在幽默室可以做什么? 
 A)  砸碎玩具以释放他们压抑的怨恨。 
 B)  只要他们重新组装,就可以把老板玩偶拆开。 
 C)  设计和安装减压装置。 
 D)  随心所欲地用力击打老板玩偶。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） Take the boss doll apart as long as they reassemble it. 
 【定位】 P4 Employees can take the doll apart as long as they put its arms and legs back in place. 
 只要把玩偶的胳膊和腿装回原位，员工就可以把它拆开。 

 【信号】 条件状语 as long as 是落点 。答案句的灵魂在 as long as they put its arms and legs back in place——as long as（只要……）是个条件限定，告诉你"可以拆，但前提是装回去"；听力里这种条件/限定词后面往往就是出题的精确落点，必须听全。 

 【替换】 take the doll apart ↔ Take the boss doll apart 拆开动作对应 
 as long as they put its arms and legs back in place ↔ as long as they reassemble it 装回=重新组装 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 Smash the toys to release their bottled-up resentments. 把 P4 的 toy store 与 P4 的 uncork their bottled-up resentments 两处原词拼在一起，但录音说的是"拆开（take apart）并装回"，绝非"砸碎（smash）"，动作被改狠了。  借用原文：uncork their bottled-up resentments 

 C) 原词陷阱 Design and install stress-reducing gadgets. 借了原文 stress-reducing gadgets 一词，但录音说这些装置是房间里现成的陈设（the room's many stress-reducing gadgets），员工是去用、不是去"设计安装（design and install）"，把现成品说成员工自造，动作主体与行为都错位。  借用原文：the room's many stress-reducing gadgets 

 D) 与原文相反 Strike at the boss doll as hard as they like. 围着真实存在的 boss doll，且 as hard as they like（想多狠就多狠）很诱人，但录音明确是 take apart（拆开）且必须 put arms and legs back in place（装回），既不是"使劲打"，更没有"随心所欲、无须复原"——条件被抹掉了。  借用原文：as long as they put its arms and legs back in place

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say has aroused public interest?
options: The recent finding of a changed gene in obese mice.
A breakthrough in understanding gene modification.
A newly discovered way for people to lose weight.
The self-repairing ability of a gene in obese mice.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the speaker say has aroused public interest? 

 【翻译】 说话者说什么引起了公众的兴趣? 
 A)  最近在肥胖小鼠体内发现的一个改变的基因。 
 B)  在理解基因修饰方面的突破。 
 C)  一种新发现的人类减肥方法。 
 D)  肥胖小鼠体内一个基因的自我修复能力。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） The recent finding of a changed gene in obese mice. 
 【定位】 P1 Public interest was aroused by the latest discovery of a changed gene in obese mice. 
 公众的兴趣是被肥胖小鼠体内一个发生改变的基因这一最新发现所引起的。 

 【信号】 题干原词 aroused 对应开篇句 。篇章开头第一句 Public interest was aroused by the latest discovery of a changed gene in obese mice. 直接出现题干里的 aroused 与 public interest，开篇点题句就是答案句。 

 【替换】 the latest discovery of a changed gene in obese mice ↔ The recent finding of a changed gene in obese mice. latest=recent、discovery=finding 

 【排除】 B) 过度推断 录音只说发现了一个改变的基因，从未称其为 A breakthrough in understanding gene modification.；breakthrough 与 gene modification 都是原文没有的拔高说法，把一次发现夸成理解上的突破，推过了头。 
 C) 偷换概念 A newly discovered way for people to lose weight. 借用了原文 discovery 的味道，却把对象从小鼠的基因偷换成给人减肥的方法；原文 a changed gene in obese mice 讲的是小鼠基因，根本没说找到了减肥办法。  借用原文：the latest discovery of a changed gene in obese mice 

 D) 原词陷阱 The self-repairing ability of a gene in obese mice. 借了 gene 与 obese mice 这些原词，但原文从未提到基因有自我修复能力，self-repairing 是凭空捏造的内容。  借用原文：a changed gene in obese mice

questions.prompt: What do we learn about the changed gene?
options: It renders an organism unable to fight diseases.
It prevents the mice's fatty tissues from growing.
It helps organisms adapt to environmental changes.
It renders mice unable to sense when to stop eating.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do we learn about the changed gene? 

 【翻译】 关于这个改变的基因我们了解到什么? 
 A)  它使生物体无法对抗疾病。 
 B)  它阻止小鼠的脂肪组织生长。 
 C)  它帮助生物体适应环境变化。 
 D)  它使小鼠无法感知何时停止进食。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） It renders mice unable to sense when to stop eating. 
 【定位】 P1 Those with the changed gene may not sense when they have eaten enough or if they have sufficient fatty tissue, and thus can't tell when to stop eating. 
 带有这个变化基因的个体，可能感知不到自己何时已吃饱、或脂肪组织是否已足够，因而无法判断该何时停止进食。 

 【信号】 因果 thus 引出后果 。句中 and thus can't tell when to stop eating 用 thus 把基因的后果点出来——感知不到饱、判断不了何时停吃，正是题干要的那个作用，因果信号词之后即答案落点。 

 【替换】 can't tell when to stop eating ↔ It renders mice unable to sense when to stop eating. can't tell=unable to sense 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 It renders an organism unable to fight diseases. 借了原文出现过的 organism 一词，但原文只说基因影响对饱腹的感知，从未提到它让生物无法抗病，fight diseases 是没说过的内容。  借用原文：tells the organism how fat or full it is 

 B) 与原文相反 It prevents the mice's fatty tissues from growing. 盗用了原文的 fatty tissue，却把意思反了——原文说的是带该基因者感知不到脂肪是否够 if they have sufficient fatty tissue，并非这个基因会阻止脂肪生长。  借用原文：if they have sufficient fatty tissue 

 C) 未提及 It helps organisms adapt to environmental changes. 又一次借用 organism，但帮助适应环境的说法原文完全没有，是凭空加上的功能。  借用原文：tells the organism how fat or full it is

questions.prompt: What does University of Vermont psychologist Esther Rothblum say?
options: Human beings have more obesity genes than most mice do.
Half of a person's total weight variation can be controlled.
People are born with a tendency to have a certain weight.
The function of the obesity genes is yet to be explored.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does University of Vermont psychologist Esther Rothblum say? 

 【翻译】 Vermont大学心理学家Esther Rothblum说了什么? 
 A)  人类拥有的肥胖基因比大多数小鼠多。 
 B)  一个人总体重变化的一半是可以控制的。 
 C)  人们天生就有保持某一体重的倾向。 
 D)  肥胖基因的功能尚待探索。 

 【答案】 C （态度观点题） People are born with a tendency to have a certain weight. 
 【定位】 P2 "This research indicates that people really are born with a tendency to have a certain weight, just as they are to have a particular skin color or height." 
 “这项研究表明，人确实生来就有形成某种体重的倾向，就像他们生来就有特定的肤色或身高一样。” 

 【信号】 人物引述原话 。原文 reacted enthusiastically: 之后是 Rothblum 的直接引语，引号内 people really are born with a tendency to have a certain weight 即她的观点，被引述人原话就是答案句。 

 【替换】 people really are born with a tendency to have a certain weight ↔ People are born with a tendency to have a certain weight. 近乎原句保留 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 Human beings have more obesity genes than most mice do. 借了原文人与鼠都有相近基因的话题，但 Rothblum 从没比较人和鼠谁的肥胖基因更多，这一数量对比原文没有。  借用原文：a gene nearly identical to the mouse obesity gene in humans 

 B) 张冠李戴 Half of a person's total weight variation can be controlled. 把第三段行为遗传学家说的 less than half of the total weight variation is programmed in the genes 安到了 Rothblum 头上，既换了说话人，又把不到一半由基因决定篡改成半数可控。  借用原文：less than half of the total weight variation is programmed in the genes 

 D) 张冠李戴 The function of the obesity genes is yet to be explored. 对应的是原文 The operation of this gene in humans has not yet been demonstrated，那是叙述者的客观补充，并非 Rothblum 的话，被错挂到她名下。  借用原文：The operation of this gene in humans has not yet been demonstrated

questions.prompt: What accounts for Americans' obesity according to a survey by the Center for Disease Control?
options: The worsening of natural environment.
The abundant provision of rich foods.
The accelerated pace of present-day life.
The adverse impact of the food industry.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What accounts for Americans' obesity according to a survey by the Center for Disease Control? 

 【翻译】 根据疾病控制中心的一项调查,美国人的肥胖归因于什么? 
 A)  自然环境的恶化。 
 B)  丰富食物的充足供应。 
 C)  当今生活节奏的加快。 
 D)  食品行业的不利影响。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） The abundant provision of rich foods. 
 【定位】 P4 Such rapid change underlines the role of environmental factors, like the abundance of rich foods, in Americans' overeating. 
 如此迅速的变化凸显了环境因素——比如丰富的高热量食物——在美国人暴饮暴食中所起的作用。 

 【信号】 underlines the role 点明成因 。原文 Such rapid change underlines the role of environmental factors, like the abundance of rich foods 用 underlines the role of 这一归因表达点出主因是环境因素，并举 rich foods 为例，正是题干要的原因。 

 【替换】 the abundance of rich foods ↔ The abundant provision of rich foods. abundance=abundant provision 

 【排除】 A) 偷换概念 The worsening of natural environment. 蹭了原文 environmental factors 里的 environmental，却把环境因素偷换成自然环境恶化；原文说的环境因素指的是食物丰富等生活环境，并非自然环境变差。  借用原文：the role of environmental factors 

 C) 未提及 The accelerated pace of present-day life. 听着合理，但这项调查归因到的是丰富食物，原文从未把肥胖归因于生活节奏加快，pace of life 是没说过的因素。 
 D) 偷换概念 The adverse impact of the food industry. 借食物话题制造与 B 的混淆，但原文归因的是 the abundance of rich foods（丰富食物本身），并没把责任算到食品工业头上，food industry 是替换上去的对象。  借用原文：the abundance of rich foods

questions.prompt: What quality do men value most concerning friendship, according to a questionnaire response?
options: Similarity in interests.
Mental stimulation.
Openness.
Compassion.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What quality do men value most concerning friendship, according to a questionnaire response? 

 【翻译】 根据问卷调查的回答，男性在友谊方面最看重什么品质? 
 A)  兴趣相似。 
 B)  智力上的激发。 
 C)  坦诚。 
 D)  同情心。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） Similarity in interests. 
 【定位】 P2 Men assigned a lower priority to them in favor of similarity in interests, selected by 77% of men, and responsiveness in a crisis, chosen by 61% male respondents. 
 男性把这些（情感类品质）排在了较低的位置，转而青睐兴趣相似——77% 的男性选了它，以及危机中的回应——61% 的男性受访者选了它。 

 【信号】 in favor of + 最高占比 77% 。信号有两层：一是 in favor of similarity in interests 这个"转而偏爱"的措辞，直接点出男性的首选；二是紧跟的最高数字 selected by 77% of men，77% 是男性各项里占比最高的，数字最高即"最看重"，双重信号锁定 similarity in interests。 

 【替换】 in favor of similarity in interests, selected by 77% of men ↔ Similarity in interests. 原词直接对应 + 最高占比佐证 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 Mental stimulation. 在录音里确实念到，但 Mental stimulation, ranked third in popularity by men 说它在男性中只排第三，是男女唯一重合项，并非"最看重"，听到这个原词就选正中陷阱。  借用原文：Mental stimulation, ranked third in popularity by men as well as women 

 C) 张冠李戴 Openness. 录音里念到，但 only 28% named openness as an important quality 说男性里只有 28% 看重它，属于女性首选的情感类品质，安到"男性最看重"头上是张冠李戴。  借用原文：Among men, only 28% named openness as an important quality 

 D) 张冠李戴 Compassion. 对应录音里的 caring，caring was picked by just 23% 说男性里仅 23% 选它，占比最低，远非男性首选，同样是女性向品质被错配给男性。  借用原文：caring was picked by just 23%

questions.prompt: What do women refer to when speaking of close friendships?
options: The willingness to offer timely help.
The joy found in each other's company.
Personal bonds.
Emotional factors.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do women refer to when speaking of close friendships? 

 【翻译】 女性在谈到亲密友谊时指的是什么? 
 A)  愿意及时提供帮助。 
 B)  在彼此陪伴中找到的快乐。 
 C)  个人纽带。 
 D)  情感因素。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） Emotional factors. 
 【定位】 P3 It is evident by their selections that when women speak of close friendships they are referring to emotional factors, while men emphasize the pleasure they find in a friend's company. 
 从她们的选择可以明显看出，女性谈到亲密友谊时指的是情感因素，而男性强调的是从朋友的陪伴中获得的乐趣。 

 【信号】 refer to 与题干对应词 + while 对比 。答案句出现题干同款动词 when women speak of close friendships they are referring to emotional factors，refer to 直接呼应题干 refer to；而 while 之后讲的是男性，构成男女对比，提醒只取 while 前面属于女性的那半句。 

 【替换】 they are referring to emotional factors ↔ Emotional factors. 原句结论词直接等于选项 

 【排除】 A) 张冠李戴 The willingness to offer timely help. 改写自录音里男性看重的 responsiveness in a crisis—"someone I can call on for help."，那是男性的特征，安给女性属张冠李戴；女性谈友谊指的是情感因素而非"危机援手"。  借用原文：they placed such strong emphasis on responsiveness in a crisis—"someone I can call on for help." 

 B) 张冠李戴 The joy found in each other's company. 几乎照搬录音 while 之后讲男性的 men emphasize the pleasure they find in a friend's company，joy=pleasure、company 原词都在，但这是男性的特征，回答"女性所指"是张冠李戴。  借用原文：men emphasize the pleasure they find in a friend's company 

 C) 未提及 Personal bonds. 听起来像和"情感"沾边，但录音讲女性时用的是 emotional factors，并未出现 personal bonds 这一表述，属未提及的近义诱饵。

questions.prompt: What may threaten a friendship for both men and women?
options: Failure to keep a promise.
Lack of frankness.
Feelings of betrayal.
Loss of contact.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What may threaten a friendship for both men and women? 

 【翻译】 什么可能对男性和女性的友谊构成威胁? 
 A)  未能信守承诺。 
 B)  缺乏坦率。 
 C)  背叛的感觉。 
 D)  失去联系。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） Feelings of betrayal. 
 【定位】 P5 As for the hazards of friendship, more than a few relationships have been shattered because of cutthroat competition and feelings of betrayal. This applies to both men and women, but unequally. 
 至于友谊的隐患，不少关系因激烈的竞争和背叛感而破裂。这一点对男女都适用，只是程度不均。 

 【信号】 hazards 主题句 + applies to both 。信号一是 As for the hazards of friendship 点出本段讲"友谊隐患"正对题干 threaten；信号二是紧接的 This applies to both men and women，applies to both 与题干 both 严丝合缝，直接圈定 competition 和 betrayal 是双方共有的威胁。 

 【替换】 feelings of betrayal ↔ Feelings of betrayal. 原句词与选项完全一致且落在 both 范围内 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 Failure to keep a promise. 听上去合理，但录音讲隐患时只点了 competition、betrayal、lack of frankness、fear of appearing unmanly，从未提"违背承诺"，属未提及。 
 B) 原词陷阱 Lack of frankness. 录音确实念到，但 men are plagued in almost equal amounts by two additional issues: lack of frankness 说这是"额外"困扰男性的问题，并非男女双方共有，与题干 both 不符，是原词陷阱。  借用原文：men are plagued in almost equal amounts by two additional issues: lack of frankness and a fear of appearing unmanly 

 D) 未提及 Loss of contact. 是最符合常识的"友谊杀手"，但录音整段讲隐患从未提及"失联"，正是预读时警惕的那个常识诱饵。

questions.prompt: Where can many of the best dinosaur specimens be found in North America?
options: Along the low-lying Colorado River.
At the Dinosaur National Monument.
Along the border of the U.S. and Canada.
At museums of natural history in large cities.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 Where can many of the best dinosaur specimens be found in North America? 

 【翻译】 在北美哪里可以找到许多最好的恐龙标本? 
 A)  沿着地势低洼的科罗拉多河。 
 B)  在恐龙国家纪念地。 
 C)  沿着美国和加拿大的边境。 
 D)  在大城市的自然历史博物馆。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） At museums of natural history in large cities. 
 【定位】 P1 Many of the best specimens may be seen today at museums of natural history in the larger cities of the United States and Canada. 
 如今许多最好的标本可以在美国和加拿大较大城市的自然历史博物馆里看到。 

 【信号】 题干关键词best specimens原样出现 。答案句开头 Many of the best specimens may be seen today 与题干 best specimens 几乎逐字对应，听到这串和题干同款的词，就知道讲者正在回答"在哪能看到"，紧跟其后的地点就是答案。 

 【替换】 at museums of natural history in the larger cities of the United States and Canada ↔ At museums of natural history in large cities 原文短语略作精简，意思不变 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 Along the low-lying Colorado River. 里的 river 是讲者后文谈骨头来历时才提到的（floated down an eastward flowing river），与"哪里能看到标本"无关，是把别处的词搬来骗"听到 river 就选"。  借用原文：floated down an eastward flowing river 

 B) 原词陷阱 At the Dinosaur National Monument. 在原文 at what is now the Dinosaur National Monument 处出现，但那是骨头被"发现"（discovered）的地方，本题问"最好的标本能在哪看到"，答非所问。  借用原文：discovered in Utah and Colorado at what is now the Dinosaur National Monument 

 C) 偷换概念 原文只说大城市分布在 the United States and Canada 两国，并未说"美加边境"，Along the border of the U.S. and Canada. 凭 United States and Canada 这串原词杜撰出 border，属偷换概念。  借用原文：the larger cities of the United States and Canada

questions.prompt: What occurs to many people when they see the massive bones in the pit wall?
options: Volcanic explosions could bring whole animal species to extinction.
Some natural disaster killed a whole herd of dinosaurs in the area.
The pit should be carefully preserved for the study of dinosaurs.
The whole region must have been struck by a devastating flood.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What occurs to many people when they see the massive bones in the pit wall? 

 【翻译】 当许多人看到坑壁上的巨大骨骼时,他们会想到什么? 
 A)  火山爆发可能导致整个动物物种灭绝。 
 B)  某种自然灾害杀死了该地区的整群恐龙。 
 C)  应该精心保护这个坑以供恐龙研究使用。 
 D)  整个地区一定遭受过毁灭性的洪水袭击。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） Some natural disaster killed a whole herd of dinosaurs in the area. 
 【定位】 P2 Many people get the idea from the mass of bones in the pit wall that some disaster such as a volcanic explosion or a sudden flood killed a whole herd of dinosaurs in this area. 
 很多人从坑壁上成堆的骨头得出一个想法：某种灾难——比如火山爆发或突发洪水——在这一带杀死了一整群恐龙。 

 【信号】 Many people get the idea直接对应题干人群 。答案句以 Many people get the idea 开头，与题干 many people 完全对上，这是"群体想法"的标志句；它说出的内容（灾难杀死整群恐龙）就是"人们会想到什么"的答案。 

 【替换】 some disaster such as a volcanic explosion or a sudden flood ↔ Some natural disaster 火山/洪水概括为natural disaster 
 killed a whole herd of dinosaurs in this area ↔ killed a whole herd of dinosaurs in the area 几乎逐字一致 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 Volcanic explosions could bring whole animal species to extinction. 借了原文真念过的 volcanic explosion，但原文说的是"杀死本地一整群恐龙"，A 却升级成"使整个物种灭绝"（whole animal species to extinction），范围被夸大，原文从未这么说。  借用原文：a volcanic explosion or a sudden flood killed a whole herd of dinosaurs 

 C) 答非所问 The pit should be carefully preserved for the study of dinosaurs. 讲"该被妥善保护以供研究"，原文虽提到 the largest and best preserved deposit，但那是描述坑保存状况好，并非说"人们看到骨头会想到要保护"，答非所问。  借用原文：the largest and best preserved deposit of dinosaurs known today 

 D) 过度推断 The whole region must have been struck by a devastating flood. 取了原文里作为举例之一的 flood，却用 must have（必然）和 whole region（整个地区）把语气和范围都拔高，原文只说洪水是人们设想的灾难"之一"，没说"全区必遭毁灭性洪水"。  借用原文：a volcanic explosion or a sudden flood killed a whole herd of dinosaurs in this area

questions.prompt: What does the speaker suggest about the large number of dinosaur bones found in the pit?
options: They floated down an eastward flowing river.
They lay buried deep in the sand for millions of years.
They were skeletons of dinosaurs inhabiting the locality.
They were remains of dinosaurs killed in a volcanic explosion.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the speaker suggest about the large number of dinosaur bones found in the pit? 

 【翻译】 关于在坑中发现的大量恐龙骨骼,说话者提出了什么看法? 
 A)  它们顺着向东流动的河流漂下来。 
 B)  它们深埋在沙土中达数百万年之久。 
 C)  它们是栖息在该地的恐龙骨架。 
 D)  它们是在火山爆发中死亡的恐龙遗骸。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） They floated down an eastward flowing river. 
 【定位】 P7 The pit area is a large dinosaur graveyard, not a place where they died. Most of the remains probably floated down an eastward flowing river until they were left on a shallow sandbar. 
 这片坑区是一座大型恐龙"墓地"，而不是它们死亡的地方。大多数遗骸很可能是顺着一条向东流的河漂下来，最后被留在了一处浅沙洲上。 

 【信号】 not a place where they died是讲者下结论的转折 。not a place where they died 用否定一句撇清"原地死亡"，紧接的 floated down an eastward flowing river 才是讲者给出的真正成因。否定+给出新说法，是讲者亮出结论的强信号。 

 【替换】 Most of the remains probably floated down an eastward flowing river ↔ They floated down an eastward flowing river. 去掉probably后几乎逐字一致 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 They lay buried deep in the sand for millions of years. 蹭了原文 half buried in the sand 的 buried/sand，但原文说的是尸体漂下后"半埋在沙里直到腐烂"，并非"深埋沙中数百万年"；deep 和 for millions of years 都是原文没有的。  借用原文：they lie, half buried in the sand, until they decay 

 C) 与原文相反 They were skeletons of dinosaurs inhabiting the locality. 说骨头是"当地栖居的恐龙"即原地死亡，但讲者明确说 not a place where they died、是漂来的"墓地"，C 取的恰是被否定的那一边，与原文相反。  借用原文：The pit area is a large dinosaur graveyard, not a place where they died. 

 D) 原词陷阱 They were remains of dinosaurs killed in a volcanic explosion. 把第 2 段大众想法里的 a volcanic explosion 搬来，但讲者全篇就是在反驳"一场灾难一次性害死"，火山致死正属被否定的旧说，D 既盗原词又站错边。  借用原文：some disaster such as a volcanic explosion or a sudden flood killed a whole herd of dinosaurs

questions.prompt: What have young Americans been accused of?
options: Indulging in seeking leisure and material comfort.
Attaching too much importance to independence.
Failing to care for parents in the traditional way.
Leaving their parents on the verge of starvation.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What have young Americans been accused of? 

 【翻译】 年轻的美国人被指责做了什么? 
 A)  沉溺于追求闲暇和物质享受。 
 B)  过分看重独立性。 
 C)  未能以传统方式照顾父母。 
 D)  让他们的父母处于饥饿的边缘。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） Failing to care for parents in the traditional way. 
 【定位】 P2 Young people in this country have been accused of not caring for their parents the way they would have in the old country. And this is true. 
 这个国家的年轻人被指责没有像在老家时那样照顾自己的父母。而这是事实。 

 【信号】 指责类信号词 accused of 直接领出答案 。录音里 have been accused of not caring for their parents 直接用了与题干同源的 accused of，后面紧跟的 not caring for their parents 就是指控内容，这种'指责词 + 后接内容'的结构是答案句的明确信号。 

 【替换】 not caring for their parents the way they would have in the old country ↔ Failing to care for parents in the traditional way not caring=Failing to care；老家方式=传统方式 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 录音确实反复讲 an American ideal of independence and autonomy，B 借这个原词诱选；但'过度看重独立'录音是用来说老人受其影响（and this is true 之后转向讲老人），并非年轻人'被指责'的那件事，属答非所问。  借用原文：an American ideal of independence and autonomy 

 A) 未提及 Indulging in seeking leisure and material comfort.（沉溺于追求休闲与物质享受）录音通篇未提及年轻人贪图享乐，纯属无中生有。 
 D) 张冠李戴 录音里 on the verge of starvation 确实出现过 starvation，D 借它诱选；但原文是说'老人自己（we）独居、濒于挨饿'，并非'年轻人害父母挨饿'，张冠李戴且把主体说反了。  借用原文：on the verge of starvation

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say about old people in the United States?
options: They have great difficulty living by themselves.
They have little hope of getting any family care.
They have fond memories of their good old days.
They have a sense of independence and autonomy.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the speaker say about old people in the United States? 

 【翻译】 说话者对美国老年人是怎么说的? 
 A)  他们独自生活有很大困难。 
 B)  他们几乎没有希望得到任何家庭照顾。 
 C)  他们对过去的美好时光有着温馨的回忆。 
 D)  他们有独立和自主意识。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） They have a sense of independence and autonomy. 
 【定位】 P2 But it is also true that old people have been influenced by an American ideal of independence and autonomy. So we live alone, perhaps on the verge of starvation, in time without friends, but we are independent. 
 但同样属实的是，老人受到了美国式独立与自主理想的影响。于是我们独自生活，也许濒于挨饿、最终没有朋友，但我们是独立的。 

 【信号】 转折 But + 结尾 but we are independent 双重强调落点 。答案句以 But it is also true 转折领出，把话题从年轻人转到老人；句末又用 but we are independent 再次转折强调'独立'，转折后的内容才是说话人真正想说的老人特征，是答案信号。 

 【替换】 we are independent ↔ a sense of independence and autonomy 形容词 independent 名词化为 independence 
 influenced by an American ideal of independence and autonomy ↔ have a sense of independence and autonomy 受独立理想影响=拥有独立自主感 

 【排除】 A) 与原文相反 录音 we live alone, perhaps on the verge of starvation 让人觉得老人'独自生活很困难'，A 借此诱选；但说话人这句的落点是 but we are independent——强调的是'独立'而非'生活困难'，A 取了转折前的表象、漏了转折后的真意。  借用原文：we live alone, perhaps on the verge of starvation 

 B) 原词陷阱 全文确有 family care 相关话题（如年轻人不照顾父母），B 借话题词诱选；但题干问的是'说话人关于老人说了什么'，本段答案句强调的是老人'独立'，并未说老人'没希望得到家庭照顾'，属答非所问。  借用原文：old people have been influenced by an American ideal 

 C) 未提及 They have fond memories of their good old days.（怀念过去的好时光）录音从未提及老人怀旧，属无中生有。

questions.prompt: What is astonishing to the young mothers interviewed by the speaker?
options: People in many parts of the world preferred small-sized families.
There have been extended families in most parts of the world.
Many elderly people were unwilling to take care of their grandchildren.
So many young Americans refused to live together with their parents.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What is astonishing to the young mothers interviewed by the speaker? 

 【翻译】 说话者采访的年轻母亲们对什么感到惊讶? 
 A)  世界许多地区的人们更喜欢小型家庭。 
 B)  世界大部分地区一直存在大家庭。 
 C)  许多老年人不愿意照顾他们的孙辈。 
 D)  这么多年轻美国人拒绝与父母住在一起。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） There have been extended families in most parts of the world. 
 【定位】 P4 They are astonished to hear that in most of the world throughout most of its history, families have been three- or four-generation families, living under the same roof. 
 她们惊讶地听到，在世界大多数地区、纵贯其大部分历史，家庭一直是三代或四代同堂、住在同一屋檐下的。 

 【信号】 惊讶标志词 astonished 直接领出答案 。录音 They are astonished to hear that 用了与题干同源的 astonished，后面 that 从句的内容就是令她们吃惊的事，这种'惊讶词 + that 从句'是答案句最明确的信号。 

 【替换】 families have been three- or four-generation families, living under the same roof ↔ There have been extended families 三四代同堂=extended families（大家庭） 
 in most of the world throughout most of its history ↔ in most parts of the world 世界大多数地区，措辞近乎同义 

 【排除】 A) 与原文相反 录音强调历史上多为大家庭，A 却说 preferred small-sized families（偏好小家庭）；说话人另有 over-emphasized the small family unit 提到 small family，A 借此原词诱选，但把'令人吃惊的事'说反了——惊讶点恰恰是'过去是大家庭'。  借用原文：over-emphasized the small family unit 

 C) 原词陷阱 全文确有祖辈与孙辈话题（如 cut off the children from their grandparents），C 借 grandchildren 诱选；但'许多老人不愿照顾孙辈'录音从未提及，且与令人吃惊的'大家庭'事实无关，属答非所问加无中生有。  借用原文：cut off the children from their grandparents 

 D) 答非所问 录音确有年轻人独立、与父母关系的内容，D 借 young Americans、live together 诱选；但题干问'令年轻母亲吃惊的事'，答案句讲的是'历史上多为大家庭'，并非'年轻美国人拒绝与父母同住'，属答非所问。  借用原文：Young people in this country have been accused

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say older people try their best to do?
options: Leave their younger generations alone.
Avoid being a burden to their children.
Stay healthy by engaging in joyful activities.
View things from their children's perspective.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the speaker say older people try their best to do? 

 【翻译】 说话者说老年人尽最大努力做什么? 
 A)  让他们的年轻一代独处。 
 B)  避免成为子女的负担。 
 C)  通过参与快乐的活动保持健康。 
 D)  从子女的角度看待事物。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） Avoid being a burden to their children. 
 【定位】 P6 So in the end, older people have to devote all their energies to "not being a burden". 
 所以到头来，老人不得不把全部精力都投入到"不成为负担"上。 

 【信号】 竭力类信号 devote all their energies to 直接领出答案 。录音 devote all their energies to "not being a burden" 用 devote all their energies to（倾尽全力于）这一'竭力'信号，与题干 try their best 同义，其后引号内的 not being a burden 即老人尽力去做的事，是答案落点。 

 【替换】 devote all their energies to "not being a burden" ↔ Avoid being a burden to their children 竭力做到'不成为负担'=尽力避免成为负担 
 the only thing they can do for their children ↔ to their children 对子女而言，对象一致 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 录音 stay out of their way 说的是父母'别挡子女的路'，A 的 Leave their younger generations alone.（别打扰晚辈）借此诱选；但题干问的是老人'尽力去做'的那件被概括的事，答案句明确落在'不成为负担'，A 只是过程中的某句铺垫，非最终落点。  借用原文：stay out of their way 

 C) 偷换概念 录音 look cheerful when they come to visit 说老人努力'显得开心'，C 借 cheerful/joyful 的近似诱选；但 C 说成 Stay healthy by engaging in joyful activities.（靠快乐活动保持健康），把'显得开心'偷换成'保持健康'，录音并未讲养生，属偷换概念。  借用原文：look cheerful when they come to visit 

 D) 张冠李戴 录音 perspective 确实出现，D 借它诱选；但原文说的是年轻人被剥夺了 perspective（视角），并非'老人努力从子女视角看问题'，主体与含义都对不上，属张冠李戴。  借用原文：Young people are being deprived of the thing they need most—perspective
